1: # Instructions
2: 
3: Creating a zipper for a binary tree.
4: 
5: [Zippers][zipper] are a purely functional way of navigating within a data structure and manipulating it.
6: They essentially contain a data structure and a pointer into that data structure (called the focus).
7: 
8: For example given a rose tree (where each node contains a value and a list of child nodes) a zipper might support these operations:
9: 
10: - `from_tree` (get a zipper out of a rose tree, the focus is on the root node)
11: - `to_tree` (get the rose tree out of the zipper)
12: - `value` (get the value of the focus node)
13: - `prev` (move the focus to the previous child of the same parent,
14:   returns a new zipper)
15: - `next` (move the focus to the next child of the same parent, returns a
16:   new zipper)
17: - `up` (move the focus to the parent, returns a new zipper)
18: - `set_value` (set the value of the focus node, returns a new zipper)
19: - `insert_before` (insert a new subtree before the focus node, it
20:   becomes the `prev` of the focus node, returns a new zipper)
21: - `insert_after` (insert a new subtree after the focus node, it becomes
22:   the `next` of the focus node, returns a new zipper)
23: - `delete` (removes the focus node and all subtrees, focus moves to the
24:   `next` node if possible otherwise to the `prev` node if possible,
25:   otherwise to the parent node, returns a new zipper)
26: 
27: [zipper]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipper_%28data_structure%29

All 14 tests pass. 

The implementation in `zipper.py` is a path-based binary tree zipper:

- **State**: each `Zipper` holds the whole tree plus a path (tuple of `"left"`/`"right"` steps) to the focus node.
- **`from_tree`** creates a zipper focused at the root (empty path); **`to_tree`** returns the stored tree.
- **`left`/`right`** extend the path, returning `None` at a dead end; **`up`** drops the last path step, returning `None` at the root.
- **`set_value`/`set_left`/`set_right`** rebuild the tree immutably — copying only the nodes along the path from the root to the focus, so the original tree and other zippers are never mutated.

One note: the spec in `.docs/instructions.md` lists rose-tree operations (`prev`, `next`, `insert_before`, `insert_after`, `delete`), but the tests — and the stub signatures — define a binary-tree API, so I implemented exactly that API. `zipper_test.py` was not modified and no new files were created.
